answer: In an agent-run orchard market, voting power follows escrowed stake, not account count: splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still buys only 100 tokens of influence. Each governance thread uses a stake snapshot, and withdrawals remain locked for 30 days, so the same funds cannot back fresh identities during that period. An attacker seeking control of the grove must acquire and immobilize real capital; generating names adds no power.
